summary: Practise gender analysis, protection risk review and safe-access planning for humanitarian programmes. Explore the five-day course and outline.
lede: Gender and protection in humanitarian settings helps humanitarian teams understand how crisis response affects people differently and reduce avoidable harm. It is for programme officers, protection specialists and field coordinators who need to adapt assistance decisions, and covers analysing access barriers, reviewing programme risks with the Gender with Age Marker and Sphere protection principles, and shaping inclusive feedback and monitoring. Exercises also address safe signposting, confidentiality limits and drafting an integrated field action plan.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for humanitarian professionals who shape, deliver or monitor assistance and need to account for gender differences, protection risks and safe access in field decisions.
modules: IASC Protection Policy in Field Decisions
IASC Gender Handbook for Context Analysis
Gender with Age Marker Evidence Review
Sphere Protection Principles in Programme Design
Core Humanitarian Standard and Safe Access
IASC GBV Guidelines and Referral Boundaries
Integrated Gender and Protection Action Plan
prerequisites: Working experience in humanitarian programming, protection, gender, accountability or a closely related field is expected. Familiarity with the humanitarian response cycle is useful. No coding or specialist software is required.
